s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive peripheral visual field blurring with corneal edema and optic disc abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive peripheral visual field blurring in both eyes
Central macular scar in the left eye
Peripheral microcystic corneal edema with central corneal sparing
key_facts: Six-month history of progressive peripheral visual field blurring
Bilateral pediatric cataract surgery at age 5
Aphakia in both eyes
Central macular scar in the left eye
Monocular right-eye vision
Family history of Fuchs’ endothelial dystrophy and microspherophakia
Wears soft monthly contact lenses
Uncorrected distance visual acuity was 20/250 OD and hand motion OS
Corrected distance visual acuity was 20/20 OD and hand motion OS
Intraocular pressures were 17 mmHg OD and 18.5 mmHg OS
Slit-lamp evaluation revealed peripheral microcystic corneal edema
Central corneal guttata present
Tilted optic disc OD
Grade 1 fundus tessellation OU
Central macular hyperpigmented scar OS

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of bilateral pediatric cataract surgery resulting in aphakia, and presents with peripheral microcystic corneal edema, which is consistent with aphakic bullous keratopathy.

rejected.label: Fuchs' endothelial dystrophy
rejected.why: While there is a family history of Fuchs' endothelial dystrophy, the patient's presentation of peripheral microcystic corneal edema and aphakia is more consistent with aphakic bullous keratopathy.

rejected.label: Pseudophakic bullous keratopathy
rejected.why: The patient is aphakic, not pseudophakic, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy
rejected.why: There is no mention of characteristic posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy findings, such as iridocorneal adhesions or corneal ectasia.

rejected.label: Congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy
rejected.why: The patient's age and presentation do not suggest a congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy, which typically presents in early childhood.
